A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central theorems, and learning framework. The main text, figures, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 1 report original simulations comparing training approaches on Gaussian single-index regression tasks.

after.justification: The original simulations are retained, and Appendix E and Table 1 add original MNIST classification experiments.

M1.justification: The central two-stage algorithm is retained. Appendix E adds a CNN classifier adaptation using cross-entropy and adversarial fine-tuning of all parameters. Full-network fine-tuning already appeared in v1's synthetic variants; the new architectural and objective choices constitute the limited method extension.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Gaussian single-index regression with ReLU, tanh, and second-Hermite targets. v2 retains these and adds MNIST classification under ℓ∞ perturbations, substantially extending the represented data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains its comparator membership. Full adversarial training and standard training followed by full adversarial training already appeared in v1 and reappear as ADV and STD + ADV on MNIST; no distinct new comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces a classification protocol reporting adversarial accuracy at ℓ∞ radii 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4. It compares 11 adversarial epochs with 10 standard plus 10 adversarial epochs, intended to approximately match computation. The original synthetic evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new MNIST comparison examines whether the pretraining advantage persists across three attack budgets, adding a limited attack-strength sensitivity analysis. The existing comparisons of known versus learned directions and frozen versus trainable first-layer weights are retained.

E5.justification: v1 states that Figure 1 averages three runs and displays shaded bands without identifying their statistic. v2 additionally reports explicit standard deviations over three runs in Table 1. This improves documented uncertainty reporting without establishing an increased run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds classification results beyond the retained synthetic findings. At ε = 0.2/0.3/0.4, STD + ADV reports accuracies of 93.80/87.2/75.3 versus 91/82/69 for ADV. These are new-setting results, not improvements over corresponding v1 measurements; Figure 1's curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds analytical counterexamples concerning dependence between coordinates and ℓ∞ attacks. Definitions 2–3 gain unit-norm requirements, the polynomial-predictor rates in Corollaries 9/11 gain polynomial-activation qualifications, and Lemma 15's norm is corrected to a squared norm. These substantively revise formal conditions and boundary analysis while retaining most proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: under the stated independence and ℓ2 assumptions, standard feature learning supplies suitable robust representations, and subsequent robust learning needs dimension-independent additional samples. Abstract edits preserve this meaning.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 newly explains why the target subspace need not remain robustly optimal outside the theorem's assumptions. Appendix E interprets MNIST results as supporting broader applicability, explains retraining all CNN parameters, and identifies which layers require adversarial training as an open question.

D1.justification: Appendix E documents the CNN's 32/64 convolutional channels, pooling and fully connected layers, PyTorch initialization, epoch budgets, batch size 64, learning rate 0.01, and pixel normalization. The existing code-access disclosure is unchanged; PGD iteration counts for the new experiment are unspecified.

R1.justification: Related work gains references on multitask representation learning and three-layer networks: CHS+24, NDL23, and WNL24. LBBH98 is added for MNIST. These modestly broaden context without redefining the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: Local edits refine the abstract, Assumption 1 discussion, and oracle explanations, and add explanations of asymptotic notation. Appendix additions and cross-references are integrated into the existing structure, with no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds the compact MNIST Table 1, places the Section 5 heading before the unchanged Figure 1, and repositions Algorithms 2–3 relative to their explanations. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: Explicit oracle conditions, the Lemma 15 correction, and MNIST results with standard deviations improve precision and empirical support. The gains remain limited: the new Appendix B.1 risk formulas omit perturbation-radius factors, and Appendix E leaves PGD iteration details unspecified. These shortcomings temper the additions without materially undermining the retained central work.
